title: Connectors Detail

options.content:
**Connectors Detail**: one collapsed row per connector, built from that connector's per-cluster boards (overview, pipeline, runtime). Expand a row for its full detail. The namespace picker applies to every row; each connector keeps its own pickers (component, pod, query type, datasource id), labelled with the connector name. Each section header links to the per-cluster board it came from.

_Generated by `tools/build-detail.py` from 21 per-cluster boards. Do not edit this board in Grafana or by hand: edit the source board and re-run the script._

### CIFS Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/cifs/cifs-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [CIFS Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-cifs-overview)

**Totals count only what happened inside the time range.** A wide range adds up every scan in it; narrow it to one scan to describe one share.

**Bars and stats say _how many_. The line charts beside them say _when_.** A scan shorter than ~30 seconds can be invisible on a line chart and still be fully counted in the bars.

**Splitting by datasource:** this board shows everything together; the Pipeline board has a datasource selector for the per-datasource view.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Totals in Window
panels.description: The summary for the selected window. Changing the time range changes every number here: these are totals, not rates.

panels.title: Files Discovered
panels.description:
**Files the scanner found and read the metadata of, in the selected range.** A file is counted once its basic metadata was read; files that could not even be read are not counted and show up as errors in the logs instead.

**Normal:** the file count of every share scanned in the range. 0 means nothing ran; the backlog panels tell idle from stuck.

**Next:** 'Items Sent' beside it — the two should match.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Items Sent
panels.description:
**Files handed on for indexing in the selected range.**

**Normal:** equal to Files Discovered. Anything less is shown in 'Item Loss'.

**Next:** 'Item Loss' beside it.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Item Loss
panels.description:
**Files found but not handed on for indexing: Files Discovered minus Items Sent.** Each such file either could not be turned into a document (bad data) or could not be handed to the sender (sender or NATS problem).

**Normal:** 0. Above 0 means those files are missing from the index while the scan still finishes.

**Next:** 'Items Failed' in the Scanner row, and 'Scanner Items by Outcome' on the Pipeline board for the cause.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) - (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Directories Forked
panels.description:
**Subfolders handed off as separate work items in the selected range.** Every subfolder found is published as its own message so other pods can scan it in parallel; this tracks the shape of the tree (number of folders), not the number of files.

**Normal:** roughly the number of folders in the scanned shares.

**Next:** 'Directories Forked vs Local' on the Pipeline board — folders that could not be handed off are walked by the same pod instead.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_directories_forked_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_directories_forked_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_directories_forked_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Content Fetches
panels.description:
**Content downloads requested in the selected range, whatever their outcome.** Content runs on its own pods and only for files someone asked to read (classification, See Content), not for the whole share.

**Normal:** whatever downstream asked for; 0 when nobody requested content.

**Next:** the Content row, and 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)' for how they ended.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Augmenter Items
panels.description:
**Items the augmenter processed in the selected range, all outcomes together.** Augment goes back to files already discovered to add permissions (ACL) and owner details.

**Normal:** the number of items sent for augment; 0 when no augment ran.

**Next:** 'Augmenter Items by Outcome (window)' in the Augmenter row.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Unit Cost — seconds per file, by stage
panels.description: What one file costs at each stage. This is capacity analysis, not incident response: it is how you predict a larger share.

panels.title: Cost per File Discovered
panels.description:
**Average scanner time per file found: total folder-processing time divided by files discovered, in the selected range.** Folder time includes listing, reading each file's metadata, the permissions query when enabled, and handing off subfolders — so trees with many folders read higher.

**Normal:** milliseconds per file. A rise with the same share means the file server or the permissions queries got slower.

**Next:** 'Directory Processing — p50 / p95 / p99' in the Scanner row.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: ACL Cost per Item Augmented
panels.description:
**Average permissions (ACL) query time per augmented item, in the selected range.** Total ACL query time divided by all items augmented — items that never reached the query (file gone, mount failed, no SMB target) are in the denominator too, so it reads lower than the true per-query cost when many items end early.

**Normal:** milliseconds. A rise means the file server is slower to answer permission queries.

**Next:** 'ACL Query — p50 / p95 / p99' in the Augmenter row.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_acl_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_acl_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_acl_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Cost per Content Fetch
panels.description:
**Average time of one content download, start to finish, in the selected range.** Failed downloads are included. It grows with file size, not file count.

**Normal:** well under a second for small files; read it together with 'Content Transfer Rate' to tell bigger files from a real slowdown.

**Next:** 'Content Transfer Rate' beside it.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Content Transfer Rate

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_uploaded_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_uploaded_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_uploaded_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 0.001)

panels.description:
**Bytes delivered per second of download time: bytes uploaded divided by the time spent in content requests, not by wall clock.** The time includes mounting the share and failed requests, so it slightly understates the raw link speed.

**Normal:** steady for the same share. Cost per fetch up with this flat = the files got bigger, nothing wrong; this falling = something genuinely got slower. Each number alone is ambiguous. Unlike 'Upload Rate', it does not drop to zero when nothing is running.

**Next:** 'Content Upload Duration' on the Pipeline board to tell a slow share read from a slow content service.

panels.title: Scanner — cifs-connector-be-go
panels.description: In: how much work is queued and why it scaled. In the middle: discovered, failed and sent, with per-directory latency.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Scanner pods currently up and being scraped.**

**Normal:** 0 between jobs is normal: the scanner scales to zero when its queue is empty (KEDA, min 0, max 10). 0 while the backlog grows means pods are not starting.

**Next:** 'Replicas' and 'NATS Backlog' in the Backlog & Autoscaling row.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Scanner container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. Restarts usually mean the pod ran out of memory (limit 1Gi) or failed its health check; a restart mid-scan can leave folders unscanned.

**Next:** the Runtime board for memory and CPU.

panels.title: Mounts Active
panels.description:
**Network shares currently mounted by the selected pods.**

**Normal:** one per datasource being worked on, back to 0 shortly after a job (mounts idle out after 60s). Stuck above 0 long after the work ended means mounts are not being released.

**Next:** 'Mount Release After Evict' on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Found
panels.description:
**Files the scanner found in the selected range.** Same count as 'Files Discovered' above, kept here next to its outcomes.

**Normal:** the file count of the scanned shares; 0 when nothing ran.

**Next:** 'Sent' and 'Failed' beside it.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description:
**Files found but not handed on for indexing in the selected range, both causes together.** Either the file's metadata could not be turned into a document (bad data) or the batch sender / NATS refused it (infrastructure).

**Normal:** 0. Any value means files missing from the index.

**Next:** 'Scanner Items by Outcome' on the Pipeline board splits the two causes.

panels.title: Sent

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="sent"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))

panels.description:
**Files handed on for indexing in the selected range.**

**Normal:** equal to 'Found'.

**Next:** 'Scanner Throughput' below for when.

panels.title: ACL Errors
panels.description:
**Permissions (ACL) queries the scanner could not complete in the selected range.** The file is still indexed, just without permissions. The scanner only queries permissions when the job enables it (skip_acl=false); the default is off, so 0 is also what a no-ACL scan shows.

**Normal:** 0. A burst points at the file server or the credential's rights to read security information.

**Next:** 'Errors by Source (window)' and the Worker Pool panels on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Dir Time p95
panels.description:
**95% of folders were processed faster than this, over the selected range.** One measurement per folder: listing it, reading each file's metadata, the permissions query when enabled, and handing off its subfolders. It does not measure a whole scan.

**Normal:** milliseconds for ordinary folders. The top folder of a large tree can take seconds because it hands off one message per subfolder.

**Next:** 'Directory Processing — p50 / p95 / p99' below for when.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.title: Scanner Throughput (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**How fast files are found, handed on, and lost, over time.** Discovered = files read; sent = handed on for indexing; failed = not handed on. Discovered always equals sent plus failed.

**Normal:** sent on top of discovered, failed at 0. A scan shorter than ~30s may barely show here; the (window) counts above have the exact numbers.

**Next:** 'Scanner Items by Outcome' on the Pipeline board, filterable per datasource.

panels.title: Directory Processing — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Time to process one folder, as typical (p50), slow (p95) and worst (p99) values over time.** One measurement per folder — listing, metadata reads, the permissions query when enabled, and handing off subfolders. It does not measure a whole scan.

**Normal:** milliseconds; p99 spikes on folders with very many entries or subfolders.

**Next:** 'Entries per Directory' and 'File Operation Duration' on the Pipeline board.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.title: Errors by Source (window)
panels.description:
**Scanner and augmenter errors by where they came from, as counts for the selected range.** Permissions (ACL) queries that failed in the scanner or in augment, SMB worker connections that could not be opened, and connections that were replaced.

**Normal:** all near 0. A few reconnects are normal on a busy share; connect errors mean the share or credential is unreachable. Scanner and augmenter ACL errors are separate counters and do not overlap.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_acl_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_acl_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_acl_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_acl_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_acl_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_acl_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_worker_connect_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_worker_connect_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_worker_connect_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_worker_reconnects_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_worker_reconnects_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_worker_reconnects_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Errors by Source (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**The same error sources as the bar beside it, over time.**

**Normal:** flat at 0. A short burst can be too small to see on a 5-minute rate; the (window) bar has the exact count.

**Next:** the Worker Pool panels on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Local Stack Depth (DFS backlog)
panels.description:
**Folders a scanner pod is walking itself because it could not hand them off as separate work.** Normally every subfolder is published as its own message; when publishing fails (typically the work stream is full) the pod keeps the folder on its own list instead. One value per pod, not split by datasource.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0 means the work stream is pushing back and the pod is carrying the tree alone — slower, but nothing is lost.

**Next:** 'Directories Forked vs Local' on the Pipeline board and 'NATS Backlog' below.

panels.title: Scanner — Backlog & Autoscaling
panels.description: How much work is waiting and whether KEDA reacted. Backlog is the cause of scaling, so it reads before the replica count.

panels.title: NATS Backlog
panels.description:
**Messages waiting in the scanner's queue (JE_CIFS / cifs-scanner-v1).** Scanner and augmenter share this one queue, so folder work and augment batches are blended and cannot be told apart here. Measured on the NATS server, so it ignores the namespace and pod selectors.

**Normal:** 0 between jobs. Growing while pods run means they are not keeping up; growing with 0 pods means scaling is not waking them.

**Next:** 'Replicas' and 'NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog'.

panels.title: NATS In Flight
panels.description:
**Messages handed to scanner pods but not yet finished (acknowledged).** This is the work currently inside the pods, and the signal KEDA's ack-capacity trigger scales on. Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** up to about 10 per pod while working (10 concurrent messages per pod), 0 when idle.

**Next:** 'KEDA — ack-capacity signal vs threshold'.

panels.title: NATS Redelivered
panels.description:
**Unfinished messages that have been delivered more than once.** A message is redelivered when a pod fails it or does not finish within the 60s ack wait. Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** 0. Growing while 'Sent' stays flat means the pods are not draining; after the 5th attempt a message goes to the dead-letter queue.

**Next:** the Dead Letter Queue row at the bottom.

panels.title: Replicas
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running right now, as KEDA's autoscaler reports.**

**Normal:** 0 with an empty queue is normal (min 0).

**Next:** 'KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max'.

panels.title: Max Replicas
panels.description:
**The most scanner pods KEDA is allowed to run.**

**Normal:** 10 by chart default. Replicas pinned here while the backlog grows means the connector is capped, not idle.

panels.title: Backlog Slope (2m)
panels.description:
**How fast the scanner queue is growing, in messages per second over the last 2 minutes (shrinking counts as 0).** This is exactly the number KEDA's trend-based trigger evaluates.

**Normal:** 0 when idle or draining. Above 0.5 KEDA asks for more pods.

**Next:** 'KEDA — trend-based signal vs threshold'.

panels.title: NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**The scanner queue over time: waiting, in progress (unacked) and redelivered.** Scanner and augmenter share this queue, so folder work and augment batches are blended. Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** a rise when a job starts, back to 0 when it ends. Waiting flat above 0 with nothing in progress means no pod is consuming.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max' beside it.

panels.title: KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running (current), what the autoscaler wants (desired), and the ceiling (max).**

**Normal:** current follows desired. Current below desired = scaling in progress or blocked; current pinned at max = capped. Scale-down is deliberately slow (cooldown 300s and a 300s stabilisation window in the chart values), so pods lingering for several minutes after a burst is configuration, not a stuck autoscaler.

**Next:** the two KEDA trigger panels beside it.

panels.title: KEDA — ack-capacity signal vs threshold
panels.description:
**KEDA's ack-capacity trigger: messages in progress against the per-pod threshold.** Pods wanted = in-progress messages ÷ 1000, rounded up; the red line is that threshold.

**Normal:** well below the line for normal jobs (each pod takes ~10 at a time), so this trigger rarely adds pods on its own.

**Next:** 'KEDA — trend-based signal vs threshold'.

panels.title: KEDA — trend-based signal vs threshold
panels.description:
**KEDA's trend-based trigger: how fast the queue grew over the last 2 minutes (only growth counts).** Threshold 0.5 messages/s, activation 0.1. The pipeline-full trigger is not created while its capacity is unset (the chart default), so this, ack-capacity and the pending-wakeup trigger are the whole scaling story.

**Normal:** spikes at the start of a large tree, when forked folders pile up faster than pods consume them.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max'.

panels.title: Augmenter — cifs-connector-be-go
panels.description: What happened to the items that came back to be enriched: how many resolved, how many were already gone, and what the ACL query cost.

panels.title: Augmenter Items by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every item the augmenter processed, as counts for the selected range.** Success = enriched with permissions; missing = the file is gone; permissions skipped = no SMB target to ask, sent without permissions; mount, stat, build, send, URN and share-mismatch failures; cancelled = dropped by a shutdown.

**Normal:** almost everything green. Yellow (missing, permissions skipped) is expected absence; orange is configuration (e.g. the credential now points at another share); red needs a look. Cancelled spikes on a shutdown and is not a real failure.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when; split per datasource on the Pipeline board.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**The augmenter's item outcomes over time.** 'missing' here is the same event as 'Skipped Not-Found' beside it — never add the two.

**Normal:** mostly success. A short augment may barely show on a 5-minute rate; the (window) bars have the exact counts.

**Next:** 'Augmenter Items by Outcome (rate, stacked)' on the Pipeline board, per datasource.

panels.title: Skipped Not-Found (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Augmented items skipped because the file no longer exists on the share.** Same event as the 'missing' outcome, not an extra one — do not add them.

**Normal:** a trickle is normal churn (files deleted between scan and augment). A large burst on one datasource suggests a share was moved or emptied.

**Next:** the Data Quality — Files Gone row.

panels.title: ACL Query — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Time of one permissions (ACL) query during augment: typical (p50), slow (p95) and worst (p99).**

**Normal:** tens of milliseconds. A rise means the file server is slow to answer security queries; augment has no pacing in front of these, so it can load the server harder than the scanner does.

**Next:** 'Augmenter ACL Query Duration' on the Pipeline board, per datasource.

panels.title: Content — cifs-connector-be-go-content
panels.description: The stage that pulls the bytes down. 0 pods with an empty queue is normal: it scales 0↔N with KEDA.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Content pods currently up and being scraped.**

**Normal:** 0 with an empty queue is normal: content scales 0↔10 on its own, independently of the scanner.

**Next:** 'Fetch Backlog' and 'KEDA — Content Replicas'.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Content container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. Restarts usually mean memory (limit 512Mi) or a failed health check; requests in flight are redelivered.

**Next:** the Runtime board with component = Content.

panels.title: Fetches
panels.description:
**Content download requests handled in the selected range, any outcome.**

**Normal:** whatever downstream asked for; 0 when nobody requested content.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)' for how they ended.

panels.title: Fetch p95 5m
panels.description:
**95% of successful content downloads finished faster than this, over the last 5 minutes.** Failed downloads are measured separately so a hung mount does not distort it.

**Normal:** seconds or less for ordinary files; it grows with file size (cap 100 MiB). A short burst may leave too few samples for a stable value.

**Next:** 'Content Fetch Duration' and 'Content Upload Duration' on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Errors
panels.description:
**Content download requests that failed in the selected range.** Includes expected cases such as files that no longer exist.

**Normal:** 0 or a few 'not found'. Anything else, or a sudden jump, needs a look.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)' for which kind of failure.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", success="false"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", success="false"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", success="false"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))

panels.title: Upload Rate
panels.description:
**Bytes per second delivered to the content service, averaged over the last 5 minutes.** This is per second of wall clock, so it drops to 0 whenever nothing is running.

**Normal:** bursty: high while a download runs, 0 otherwise.

**Next:** 'Content Transfer Rate' at the top for speed while actually transferring.

panels.title: Mount p95 5m
panels.description:
**95% of successful share mounts on content pods finished faster than this, over the last 5 minutes.** Failed mounts are measured separately, so a mount that hangs ~120s before failing does not distort this number.

**Normal:** near 0 when the share is already mounted; up to a second or two for a fresh mount.

**Next:** 'Content Mount Acquire p95 — success vs failure' on the Pipeline board.

panels.title: Fetch Backlog
panels.description:
**Content requests waiting in the queue, bulk and interactive (See Content) together.** Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** 0 between requests. Growing with 0 content pods means scaling is not waking them.

**Next:** 'NATS — Content Consumer Backlog'.

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When content downloads happened and how the outcomes interleaved.** Read the time axis; the height is a rate and looks vanishingly small, because a burst of a few downloads in seconds divided over five minutes is a fraction per second. 'NONE' from the connector is shown as success.

**Normal:** mostly success. For how many ended each way, read the bar beside it. Counting per time bucket was tried on the Box board and rejected: it under-counts when the whole burst lands in one bucket.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)' beside it.

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (window)

targets.expr: (sum by (error_code) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) > 0

panels.description:
**How the content downloads in the selected range ended, as counts.** This answers 'I ran N downloads — what happened to them?'; the total is in 'Fetches'.

**Normal:** green (success) dominates. Yellow is expected (the file is gone, nothing to do), orange is back-pressure or a transient problem that is retried, red needs action (permissions, credentials, internal errors).

**Next:** 'Fetch Errors by error_code' on the Pipeline board, per datasource.

panels.title: Uploaded Bytes (rate)
panels.description:
**Bytes per second delivered to the content service, over time.**

**Normal:** bursts while downloads run, 0 between them.

**Next:** 'Content Transfer Rate' at the top.

panels.title: Content Requests In-Flight
panels.description:
**Content requests being worked on right now, per pod.** The content side's saturation signal; the real queue is on the NATS server.

**Normal:** up to 10 per pod (10 workers). Pinned at 10 while the queue grows means the pods are at capacity and KEDA should be adding more.

**Next:** 'NATS — Content Consumer Backlog'.

panels.title: NATS — Content Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**The content queue over time: requests waiting and in progress (unacked).** Bulk and interactive (See Content) queues together. Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** rises when downloads are requested, back to 0 when done.

**Next:** 'KEDA — Content Replicas' and 'Content Requests In-Flight'.

panels.title: NATS — Content Consumer Redelivery
panels.description:
**Content requests delivered more than once.** Transient failures (timeout, connection, read or upload errors) are retried. Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** 0. Growing means downloads are failing and retrying; after 3 deliveries (maxDeliver 3) a request is dropped for good.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome (window)' for why.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Content pods running (current), what the autoscaler wants (desired), and the ceiling (max).** Content scales on its own trigger, watching the content queue, independently of the scanner.

**Normal:** current follows desired, 0 when idle. Pinned at max (10) while the queue grows means capped. Scale-down is slow by design (cooldown 300s, 300s stabilisation).

**Next:** 'KEDA — Content Trigger Signals'.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Trigger Signals
panels.description:
**The numbers behind the content autoscaler: requests in progress, queue growth over 2 minutes, and requests waiting.** Bulk and interactive queues together; the interactive one has its own wake-up trigger so a single See Content click wakes a pod. Measured on the NATS server (no namespace/pod filter).

**Normal:** all 0 when idle. Waiting above 0 should bring a pod up within a polling interval (30s).

**Next:** 'KEDA — Content Replicas'.

panels.title: Data Quality — Files Gone
panels.description: How many files are gone, and which path found that out. Do not add the stages together: they are different moments in the pipeline.

panels.title: Gone at Augment (404)
panels.description:
**Items augment went back for and found gone from the share, in the selected range.** Its own stage only — content 404s are no longer added in, which used to make a run with no augment still show a count.

**Normal:** a small number is normal churn between scan and augment.

**Next:** 'Files Gone % (augment)' for the share of the total.

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="missing"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Gone — 404 on content fetch

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Content downloads that found the file gone, in the selected range.** The latest point of all: the file disappeared between the scan and the download. On CIFS this code also covers things that are not regular files (symlinks, sockets, devices), so it shows the content is not retrievable rather than proving deletion.

**Normal:** a few. Do not add this to the augment count — content runs on demand over a subset of files, so it has a different denominator.

**Next:** 'Gone by Stage' for when.

panels.title: Augment Items

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0))

panels.description:
**Items augment visited in the selected range: the denominator for the percentage beside it.** 50% of 6 items and 50% of 60,000 are the same number and very different news. This counts only what augment visited, never the whole share.

**Normal:** the size of the augment batches run in the range.

**Next:** 'Files Gone % (augment)' beside it.

panels.title: Files Gone % (augment)
panels.description:
**Share of augmented items whose file was already gone, in the selected range.** Augment only: content fetches one file per request and has no comparable denominator.

**Normal:** a few percent at most. A high value on one datasource suggests the share was reorganised or emptied since the scan.

**Next:** 'Augment Items' beside it for the count behind the percentage.

targets.expr: 100 * ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="missing"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", outcome="missing"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) or vector(0)), 1))

panels.title: Gone by Stage (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Files found missing, split by the stage that noticed, over time.** Augment and content are different moments and are diagnosed differently. The content line also counts non-regular files (symlinks, sockets, devices).

**Normal:** near 0. A short burst may barely show on a 5-minute rate; the stats beside it have the exact counts.

**Next:** 'Skipped Not-Found' in the Augmenter row.

panels.title: Data Loss — Dead Letter Queue
panels.description: What was lost. The scanner funnel can close perfectly and work can still have been discarded here: a message that exhausts its deliveries ends up in the DLQ leaving no trace in items_processed.

panels.title: DLQ Depth
panels.description:
**Messages currently stored in the dead-letter queue: work the system gave up on after 5 failed attempts.** Each one is a folder (with everything below it) or an augment batch that was dropped, while the scan still reports success because it never got far enough to count as a failure. The stored count can fall when the queue is purged or trimmed at its size limit.

**Normal:** 0. Any value above 0 is silently lost work.

**Next:** 'Lost to DLQ (window)' for what was added in the range.

panels.title: Lost to DLQ (window)
panels.description:
**Messages that failed every attempt and were given up on in the selected range.** Each one is a folder — and everything below it — or an augment batch that was not processed, while its scan still reported success.

**Normal:** 0. Each message carries the directory or batch and the last error: `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_CIFS <seq>`. Counted from the stream's sequence number, so a purge or the queue's size limit does not hide anything.

**Next:** 'DLQ Depth over time' beside it, for when it started.

panels.title: DLQ Depth over time
panels.description:
**The dead-letter queue size over time.** A step up is the moment work was dropped.

**Normal:** flat at 0. Line a step up against the scanner throughput: that chart will not show a dip, which is exactly why this row exists.

**Next:** 'NATS Redelivered' to see the retries that came before.

options.content:
### CIFS Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/cifs/cifs-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [CIFS Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-cifs-pipeline)

**This is the drill-down.** The Overview says *what happened*; this board says *where, for which datasource, and at what cost*. Use the datasource selector at the top to narrow everything to one datasource.

**Totals count only what happened inside the time range** — narrow it to one scan to describe one share.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Scanner — Discovery & Throughput
panels.description: How fast it discovers, and whether anything is lost between discovering and sending.

panels.title: Scanner Items by Outcome (rate)
panels.description:
**What happened to each file the scanner found, over time, against the discovery rate.** Sent = handed on for indexing; marshal_failed = the file's metadata could not be turned into a document (bad data); batch_send_failed = the sender or NATS refused it (infrastructure). The outcomes always add up to discovered. Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** everything sent. A scan shorter than ~30s may barely show on this rate; the Overview's (window) counts have the exact numbers.

**Next:** the error stream / logs for the paths; bad data and infrastructure failures are fixed in different places.

panels.title: Directories Forked vs Local (rate)
panels.description:
**Subfolders handed off as separate work (forked) versus walked by the same pod (local), over time.** A folder is only walked locally when handing it off failed — usually because the work stream is full. Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** local at 0. Local above 0 means back-pressure on the work stream: the pod carries the tree alone, slower, but nothing is lost.

**Next:** 'Local Stack Depth' below and 'NATS Backlog' on the Overview.

panels.title: Entries per Directory — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**How many entries one folder holds: typical (p50), large (p95) and largest (p99).** Files and subfolders both count, so it reads higher than a folder's file count. One measurement per folder. Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** depends on the share. Very large folders explain slow p99 in 'Directory Processing'.

**Next:** 'Directory Processing — p50 / p95 / p99'.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_files_per_scan_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.title: Discovery → Sent Conversion
panels.description:
**Share of found files that were handed on for indexing.**

**Normal:** 100%. Below means files are being lost between discovery and send. It shows a gap while nothing is being discovered.

**Next:** 'Scanner Items by Outcome' for the cause.

panels.title: Item Loss (discovered − sent)
panels.description:
**Files lost between discovery and send, per second (found minus sent).**

**Normal:** 0. Sustained above zero means files are not reaching the sender.

**Next:** 'Scanner Items by Outcome' says which of the two causes.

panels.title: Scanner — Workers & File Operations
panels.description: Where the time goes inside a directory, and whether workers are waiting rather than working.

panels.title: File Operation Duration p95 by operation
panels.description:
**95th-percentile time of each per-file step: reading file metadata (lstat), looking up the owner name, and building the document.** Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds. A slow metadata read means the file server is slow; a slow owner lookup means name resolution is.

**Next:** 'Directory Processing — p50 / p95 / p99'.

panels.title: Worker Pool — busy / pool size / channel depth
panels.description:
**The scanner's permissions (ACL) worker pool: workers busy, pool size, and requests waiting in its queue.** Only used when the job enables permissions (skip_acl=false); otherwise all flat. Pool size is CPUs × 50 (poolSizePerCPU) — about 100 at the 500m CPU limit — and the queue holds 16× that.

**Normal:** busy below pool size and the queue mostly empty. Busy pinned at the pool size with a full queue means the file server's permission queries are the bottleneck.

**Next:** 'Work Channel Wait p95' and 'Scanner ACL Query Duration'.

panels.title: Scanner ACL Query Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Time of one permissions (ACL) query from the scanner: typical (p50), slow (p95) and worst (p99).** Only when the job enables permissions (skip_acl=false); flat otherwise. Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** tens of milliseconds. Rises mean the file server answers security queries slowly.

**Next:** 'Worker Pool' and the Overview's 'Errors by Source'.

panels.title: Work Channel Wait p95 — submit vs collect
panels.description:
**How long the scanner waited to queue a permissions request (submit) and to get a result back (collect), 95th percentile.**

**Normal:** both near 0. High submit wait = the worker queue is full; high collect wait = workers are slow to answer, i.e. the file server.

**Next:** 'Worker Pool — busy / pool size / channel depth'.

panels.title: Local Stack Depth (DFS backlog)
panels.description:
**Folders a scanner pod is walking itself because it could not hand them off.** One value per pod, not split by datasource.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0 means the work stream is pushing back (it holds up to 1 GiB and refuses new messages when full).

**Next:** 'Directories Forked vs Local'.

panels.title: Directory Processing — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Time to process one folder: typical (p50), slow (p95) and worst (p99).** One measurement per folder — listing, metadata reads, the permissions query when enabled, and handing off subfolders. It does not measure a whole scan. Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** milliseconds for ordinary folders; the top folder of a big tree can take seconds because it hands off one message per subfolder.

**Next:** 'Entries per Directory' and 'File Operation Duration'.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) - last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(cifs_scanner_scan_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.title: Scanner — Mounts & Data Quality
panels.description: Whether the SMB mount is the bottleneck, and how much of what reports success is degraded success.

panels.title: Mount Release After Evict (rate)
panels.description:
**Releases of a share mount that had already been dropped (for example because it died mid-batch).** Several items finishing against a dead mount each release it once; this is informative, not a bug. Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** 0 or rare. Frequent bursts mean mounts keep dying under load.

**Next:** 'Augmenter Mount Acquire' and 'Content Mount Acquire' for failed mounts.

panels.title: Btime Unavailable (rate)
panels.description:
**Files whose real creation time was not available, so 'Created' fell back to the last-change time.**

**Normal:** 0 per datasource. Steady counts on one datasource = that file server does not report creation time (older Samba, some NAS); every datasource at once = the node's kernel is too old. Only this panel tells whether 'Created' is real.

**Next:** split per datasource with the selector.

panels.title: Augmenter — Outcomes & Mounts
panels.description: The augment breakdown: outcome by type, and what acquiring the mount costs.

panels.title: Augmenter Items by Outcome (rate, stacked)
panels.description:
**Every augment outcome over time, stacked.** success, missing (file gone), stat_failed, acl_error, acl_skipped (no SMB target — sent without permissions), build_failed, send_failed, invalid_urn, mount_failed, unc_mismatch (the credential now points at a different share; item skipped), cancelled_stat / cancelled_acl (dropped by a shutdown, not a real failure). Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** almost all success. unc_mismatch means someone re-pointed a credential; mount_failed means the share is unreachable.

**Next:** the Overview's 'Augmenter Items by Outcome (window)' for exact counts.

panels.title: Augmenter Mount Acquire p95 — success vs failure
panels.description:
**95th-percentile time to mount the share during augment, successful and failed mounts shown separately.** Kept apart so a mount that hangs ~120s before failing does not distort the success line.

**Normal:** success near 0 when already mounted, up to a second or two for a fresh mount; failure line absent.

**Next:** the 'mount_failed' outcome in 'Augmenter Items by Outcome'.

panels.title: Augmenter Publish Blocked — p99
panels.description:
**Worst-case (p99) time augment workers waited for their turn to publish items.** Workers share one sender; every so often a publish goes to NATS and everyone else waits, for up to 5 minutes if the stream is full. Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** milliseconds. Hundreds of milliseconds or more means back-pressure from the stream.

**Next:** 'NATS Backlog' on the Overview.

panels.title: Augmenter Errors (rate)
panels.description:
**Augment permission-query errors and files skipped because they are gone, per second.** The permissions series is not split by datasource; the not-found series follows the selector. A failed permission query still sends the item, without permissions.

**Normal:** permission errors at 0; a trickle of not-found is normal churn.

**Next:** 'Augmenter Items by Outcome' for the full picture.

panels.title: Augmenter ACL Query Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Time of one permissions (ACL) query during augment: typical (p50), slow (p95) and worst (p99).** Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** tens of milliseconds; rises mean the file server answers slowly.

**Next:** 'Augmenter Errors' if queries start failing.

panels.title: Content — Fetch & Streaming
panels.description: Latency and volume of the download. The percentiles average 1KiB and 1GiB files together — read effective throughput before concluding anything got slower.

panels.title: Content Fetches by error_code (rate, stacked)
panels.description:
**Content downloads per second by result code, stacked.** NONE is success. FETCH_ERROR_* are classified failures (not found, permission denied, too large, timeout…); NAK_* are messaging failures where the request could not be read or the reply could not be sent, and it is retried.

**Normal:** almost all NONE. A short burst may barely show on a 5-minute rate; the Overview's (window) bar has exact counts.

**Next:** 'Fetch Errors by error_code' below.

panels.title: Content Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**End-to-end time of one successful content download: typical (p50), slow (p95) and worst (p99).** Failed downloads are recorded separately and left out, so a slow failure does not distort these. Filtered by the datasource selector.

**Normal:** seconds or less; grows with file size.

**Next:** 'Content Upload Duration' to tell share reading/upload from mounting.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.title: Content Fetch Bytes — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Size of successfully downloaded files: typical (p50), large (p95) and largest (p99).** Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** depends on the share; files above 100 MiB are refused as too large.

**Next:** 'Content Latency per MiB' and 'Average Bytes per Fetch'.

panels.title: Content Mount Acquire p95 — success vs failure
panels.description:
**95th-percentile time to mount the share for a content download, successful and failed mounts shown separately.** Kept apart so a mount that hangs ~120s before failing does not distort the success line.

**Normal:** near 0 when already mounted, up to a second or two for a fresh mount; failure line absent.

**Next:** 'Fetch Errors by error_code' for connection failures.

panels.title: Fetch Errors by error_code (increase, 1h)
panels.description:
**Failed content downloads in the last hour, by result code.** NAK_* codes are messaging failures (request unreadable, reply not sent) and are retried; FETCH_ERROR_* are classified failures. Timeouts, connection, read and upload errors are retried up to 3 times; the rest are final.

**Normal:** empty or a few FETCH_ERROR_NOT_FOUND (which on CIFS also covers symlinks and other non-regular files).

**Next:** the per-datasource p95 panels below.

panels.title: Content Upload Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Time of the read-from-share + send-to-content-service step of a successful download: p50, p95, p99.** Isolated from mounting and the rest of the request, so a slow content service can be told apart from a slow share read.

**Normal:** most of the download time for large files.

**Next:** 'Content Fetch Duration' — if that rises and this does not, the extra time is in mounting or messaging.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(cifs_content_upload_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(cifs_content_upload_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(cifs_content_upload_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.title: Content Fetch p95 by datasource_id

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, datasource_id) (rate(cifs_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**95th-percentile successful download time, one line per datasource.**

**Normal:** similar lines for similar shares. One line far above the rest points at that share or its file server.

**Next:** 'Content Upload p95 by datasource_id' beside it.

panels.title: Content Upload p95 by datasource_id

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, datasource_id) (rate(cifs_content_upload_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$cifs_pod", datasource_id=~"$cifs_datasource_id", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description:
**95th-percentile read-and-upload time of successful downloads, one line per datasource.**

**Normal:** similar lines for similar shares. One datasource high here but not in mount time means reading that share is slow.

**Next:** 'Content Mount Acquire' for mounting time.

panels.title: Content Latency per MiB (interim)
panels.description:
**Read-and-upload time per MiB delivered, successful downloads only.** Total read-and-upload time divided by total bytes in each 5-minute window, so many small files and one large file land on the same point, and fixed per-file overhead makes small files look expensive. Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** steady. Flat while download time climbs means the cost is per request, not per byte.

**Next:** 'Average Bytes per Fetch' beside it.

panels.title: Average Bytes per Fetch
panels.description:
**Average size of a successfully downloaded file.** Not filtered by datasource.

**Normal:** depends on the share. Pair it with the panel on the left: a latency jump with flat size is a slowdown; one that tracks size is just bigger files.

**Next:** 'Content Latency per MiB'.

options.content:
### CIFS Connector — Runtime
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/cifs/cifs-runtime.json` · per-cluster board: [CIFS Connector — Runtime](/d/apps-v2-cifs-runtime)

**Is the connector itself healthy?** CPU, memory, Go runtime and file handles for the scanner and content pods. Use the *component* selector at the top to look at one of them.

**Empty is normal:** both deployments scale to zero between jobs, so this board only has data while something runs.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it shows, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Process — CPU & Memory
panels.description: Whether the process keeps growing or settles.

panels.title: Process CPU (rate)
panels.description:
**CPU used by the connector process, per pod (1 = 100% = one full core).**

**Normal:** the scanner is limited to 500m (50%) and content to 250m (25%). Sitting at the limit during a job means the pod is throttled and runs slower.

**Next:** 'Container CPU Usage' for the container's view.

panels.title: Process Resident Memory
panels.description:
**Memory actually held in RAM by the connector process, per pod.**

**Normal:** rises during a job and settles afterwards. The limit is 1 GiB for the scanner and 512 MiB for content; reaching it gets the pod killed and restarted.

**Next:** 'Heap In-Use' to see whether it is Go data or something else.

panels.title: Process Virtual Memory
panels.description:
**Address space reserved by the process, per pod.** Mostly reservations, not real memory use, so it is far larger than resident memory.

**Normal:** large and flat. Only steady growth over many jobs is worth a look.

**Next:** 'Process Resident Memory' for real usage.

panels.title: Container — Resource Usage
panels.description: The same seen from the cgroup: this is what decides an OOMKill, not what the process reports.

panels.title: Container CPU Usage
panels.description:
**CPU used by each CIFS pod's containers (1 = 100% = one full core).** Covers scanner and content pods regardless of the component selector.

**Normal:** below the limit: 500m (50%) for the scanner, 250m (25%) for content. Flat at the limit means the pod is throttled.

**Next:** 'Process CPU' for the process alone.

panels.title: Container Memory (working set)
panels.description:
**Memory the kernel counts against each CIFS pod (working set), the number used to decide out-of-memory kills.** Covers scanner and content pods regardless of the component selector.

**Normal:** below the limit: 1 GiB for the scanner, 512 MiB for content. Climbing to it ends in a restart.

**Next:** 'Restarts (1h)' on the Overview.

panels.title: Go Runtime
panels.description: Goroutines and GC. A goroutine count that rises and never falls is a leak, not load.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description:
**Concurrent tasks (goroutines) inside the process, per pod.**

**Normal:** rises with work — the scanner runs up to ~100 permission workers per datasource when permissions are enabled — and returns to a low base afterwards. A base that keeps climbing between jobs is a leak.

**Next:** 'OS Threads' and 'Heap In-Use'.

panels.title: Heap In-Use
panels.description:
**Memory held by live Go data, per pod.**

**Normal:** rises during a job and drops after garbage collection. Close to resident memory is normal; much lower means the rest is outside Go (e.g. the kernel mount).

**Next:** 'Process Resident Memory'.

panels.title: GC Pause — max & median
panels.description:
**How long the program pauses to clean up memory, per pod.** Max = the longest pause, median = a typical one. (This panel used to ask for a p99, which this metric cannot provide — it always came back empty.)

**Normal:** a few milliseconds. Pauses of hundreds of milliseconds mean memory pressure and stall everything the pod is doing.

**Next:** 'Heap In-Use' — bigger heaps take longer to clean.

panels.title: File Descriptors & Threads
panels.description: Whether it is approaching the descriptor limit, which in a file connector is a real ceiling.

panels.title: Open vs Max FDs
panels.description:
**Open files and network connections (file descriptors) against the per-process maximum, per pod.**

**Normal:** far below the maximum, back to a low base after a job. Open climbing toward max means connections or files are not being closed, and new SMB connections will start failing.

**Next:** 'Errors by Source' on the Overview for connection failures.

panels.title: OS Threads
panels.description:
**Operating-system threads used by the process, per pod.**

**Normal:** a few tens and stable. Threads grow when calls block in the kernel — e.g. reads from an unresponsive share — so a jump here during a job points at a hung mount.

**Next:** 'Mount Acquire' panels on the Pipeline board.

options.content:
### MySQL Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/mysql/mysql-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [MySQL Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-mysql-overview)

panels.title: Connections (Open)
panels.description: Open MySQL connections summed across every active scanner pool. Pools are per-datasource and created/evicted at runtime, so this is a scrape-time aggregate, not a fixed ceiling.

panels.title: ScanStart In Flight
panels.description: ScanStart handler invocations currently doing database discovery and DatabaseFork fan-out. The per-table leaf work that runs after fan-out is counted separately (see Tables In Flight on the pipeline dashboard).

panels.title: Items Sent (5m)
panels.description: Items successfully submitted through ItemBatchSender.UpsertItem, per second.

panels.title: Scan p95 (5m)
panels.description: p95 of the ScanStart discovery + fan-out phase. Histogram ladder is 0.5s to ~1024s, so this measures how long it takes to enumerate databases and hand out work — not how long a whole scan takes end to end.

panels.title: Error Rate (5m)
panels.description: Query failures against the source database, per second: database_errors_total + table_errors_total. Skipped tables and connector bugs are counted apart — see the Silent-Failure Signals row.

panels.title: Table Panics (5m)
panels.description: Leaf-worker tasks that panicked. Always a connector bug, never a source-database fault — counted apart from table_errors_total so a panic on an unexpected column shape doesn't read as the customer's MySQL refusing a query. Any non-zero value is worth acting on.

panels.title: Inline Fallback (5m)
panels.description: Tables the worker pool refused, run inline on the NATS consumer goroutine instead of being dropped. The pool only refuses after Shutdown, so non-zero means a scan was still fanning out while the process was tearing down — accounting stays exact, but the rest of that database serialises onto one goroutine.

panels.title: No Visible Columns (5m)
panels.description: Tables skipped because INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS returned no rows — a missing column-level GRANT, or a table dropped mid-scan. The query succeeded, so this is not a query failure. Alert on a sustained rate, not on any non-zero value.

panels.title: Error Reports Dropped (5m)
panels.description: Structured errors that never reached the observer, across all reasons (buffer_full, after_close, publish_failed). Non-zero means the job record is showing a truncated view of the scan's failures. Break down by reason on the pipeline dashboard.

panels.title: Connections (Open)
panels.description: Open MySQL connections summed across active content-fetch pools. A climb that does not come back down alongside a non-zero Conn Discard failure is the pool-exhaustion signature described on that panel.

panels.title: Fetch In Flight
panels.description: Content fetch requests currently being processed.

panels.title: Fetch p95 (5m)
panels.description: p95 end-to-end fetch latency for successful requests only: handler entry (URN parse, datasource resolve, conn acquire) through stream completion and reply publish. Errors are filtered out so a fast failure doesn't flatter the number.

panels.title: Errors (5m)
panels.description: Content requests that errored in the last 5 minutes — counter increase on mysql_content_requests_total{outcome="error"}.

panels.title: Content Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
Producer Panics (5m)
panels.description: Streaming producers that panicked and were recovered. Always a connector bug: the requester is told INTERNAL/retryable and the message is redelivered, so nothing in the request's own outcome says this connector crashed.

panels.title: Byte Mismatch (5m)
panels.description: Uploads whose stored size disagreed with the sampled/streamed byte count. The handler NAKs without replying, so a single count is a transient that a redelivery repaired; a sustained rate means the same URN fails verification every attempt, and once MaxDeliver is spent the object proven wrong stays under that URN with no reply ever sent.

panels.title: Conn Discard Failures (5m)
panels.description: Abandoned result sets whose connection could NOT be discarded (outcome != "discarded"). The discard is the only defence against the driver's uncancellable drain of the rest of a multi-GB column — a drain that ignores the query deadline and SIGTERM while holding a pool connection and a worker slot. Non-zero means the byte budget stops bounding what crosses the wire, and the symptom surfaces as pool exhaustion rather than an error.

panels.title: Sample Re-draws (5m)
panels.description: Content fetches whose first random draw fell under MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS and were re-drawn at a higher percent, all outcomes summed. Each re-draw is an extra table scan, so a sustained rate means MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT is set too low for the tables being classified — raise the percent, not the floor. Break down by outcome on the pipeline dashboard: "failed" is a different problem and points at the query timeout and the source database.

options.content:
### MySQL Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/mysql/mysql-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [MySQL Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-mysql-pipeline)

panels.title: Tables & Columns Discovered (rate)
panels.description: Tables successfully scanned and columns retrieved, per second. Tables that failed or were skipped are not in these counters — see the Errors & Silent Failures row.

panels.title: Items & Batches Sent (rate)
panels.description: items/s is the connector's own mysql_scanner_items_sent_total. The other two come from the shared ItemBatchSender in pipeline-lib-go and carry no connector prefix, so they are filtered by job — batches/s is how often the batch is flushed to JobEngine.

panels.title: Scan Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: ScanStart database discovery + fan-out phase, on a 0.5s–1024s ladder. This runs on the single pod that received the ScanStart message; the leaf work it hands out is not included.

panels.title: Scanner Errors (rate)
panels.description: Query failures against the source database. These are the only two counters that mean "MySQL refused something" — everything on the next two panels is deliberately kept out of them.

panels.title: Skips & Connector Bugs (count, 5m)
panels.description: Three failure modes counted apart from table_errors_total because none of them is the source database's fault. no visible columns — INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS returned nothing (missing column-level GRANT, or a table dropped mid-scan); alert on a sustained rate, not any non-zero value. inline fallback — the worker pool refused a table after Shutdown and the scanner ran it on the consumer goroutine, serialising the rest of that database. table panics — always a connector bug, any non-zero value is worth acting on.

panels.title: Error Reporter Drops by Reason (count, 5m)
panels.description: Structured errors that never reached the observer, so the job record is showing a truncated view of the scan's failures. buffer_full — the buffered channel saturated. after_close — PublishError called after Close. publish_failed — the observer refused or could not be reached; this is the remote failure mode, and without it an unreachable observer used to lose every ItemError while the drop counter stayed at zero. close timeouts counts one abandonment of an unknown number of reports rather than individual errors, which is why it is a separate series: reaching it means publishLoop was parked inside a single publish for the whole flush budget, so check the control plane's health, not the scan.

panels.title: Error Reporter — Abandoned Flushes (live)
panels.description: Abandoned error-reporter flushes whose background goroutine is still parked in a publish — a live count on this pod, not a rate. Its sibling on the panel to the left counts how many times an abandonment has happened since the pod started; this one is how many are outstanding right now, which is the number that says whether the pod is still healthy. The two differ because an ErrorReporter is built and closed per message (one per ScanStart, one per DatabaseFork): an abandoned flush leaves a goroutine plus its 100-slot buffer behind, and the error that Close's caller returns NAKs the message, so redelivery supplies another fork that does it again. It unwinds on its own — each goroutine exits as soon as its publish returns — so a value that climbs and stays up is a control plane that is not answering, not a leak the connector can close from the inside. On the pinned pipeline-lib-go that publish resolves the job's step through GetJobSettings on a context with no deadline, which is why there is nothing bounding it below the reporter's 5s flush budget. Sustained above zero is alert-worthy; check the control plane, not the scan.

panels.title: Query Duration Heatmap
panels.description: Scanner-path SQL latency distribution, on a 10ms–20s ladder.

panels.title: Query p95 by query_type
panels.description: query_type is list_tables (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES per database) or query_columns (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS per table). A list_tables p95 climbing alone points at a database with a very wide table count; query_columns climbing points at the tables themselves.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, query_type) (rate(mysql_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$mysql_pod", query_type=~"$mysql_query_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: Scanner Connections by Type
panels.description: Aggregated across every active scanner pool at scrape time. in-use pinned at open with idle at zero is the pool running at its ceiling.

panels.title: Scanner — In Flight
panels.description: scanstart is the discovery + fan-out phase on the pod that received ScanStart. tables (leaf pool) is the per-table work the fan-out handed to the worker pool — the two are counted separately on purpose, so a busy leaf pool does not look like a stuck ScanStart.

panels.title: Query Rate by query_type
panels.description: Observation count on the query-duration histogram — how many scanner-path queries are actually being issued, split by kind.

panels.title: Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99 by outcome
panels.description: End-to-end request latency, split by outcome so a fast failure does not flatter the success distribution: handler entry (URN parse, datasource resolve, conn acquire) through stream completion and reply publish.

panels.title: Stream Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The streaming pipeline only — from the producer goroutine pulling its first row out of MySQL until UploadFrom returns. Excludes handler setup. Query and upload run concurrently, so this reflects whichever leg is slower at any moment; the gap between this and Fetch Duration is setup cost.

panels.title: Stream Bytes — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Bytes per successful fetch, taken from UploadResponse.Size — the count the content transfer service actually stored, not Info.Size, which this connector leaves at 0 because a sample's length is unknown until the last row streams. Ladder runs 1KiB to 4GiB.

panels.title: Stream Throughput (bytes/s)
panels.description: Sum of stored bytes per second across successful fetches.

panels.title: Stream Rows — Rate (rows/s)
panels.description: Sampled rows written per second across successful fetches.

panels.title: Stream Rows — Avg per Fetch
panels.description: Average sampled rows per successful fetch (sum / count over the window). Compare against MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS and MAX_ROWS: sitting at the ceiling means the sampler is being capped, sitting at the floor means it is being rescued by re-draws.

panels.title: Sample Re-draws by Outcome (count, 5m)
panels.description: Fetches whose first draw fell under MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS and were re-drawn at a higher percent. recovered — a later draw reached the floor. short — every draw stayed under it, and since the final draw runs at 100% that means the column genuinely holds fewer non-NULL values than the floor, not a sampling miss. failed — a draw errored before finishing, so its row count says nothing about the column; kept separate so a broken query is not read as a small column. A fourth case carries no label and appears in none of these: a draw torn down because the upload died. During a content-service outage the three series therefore do not sum to the number of fetches that re-drew. Sustained recovered/short means raise MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT, not the floor — each re-draw is an extra table scan. Sustained failed is a different problem: look at the query timeout and the source database.

panels.title: Sample Percent Used
panels.description: The percent the streamed draw actually ran at. It equals MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT whenever the first draw was kept, so drift above the configured value is the signal that the row floor is doing the work instead of the percent.

panels.title: Conn Discard by Outcome (count, 5m)
panels.description: Abandoned result sets whose driver connection was thrown away rather than drained. discarded — the connection was closed so the driver skips its post-finish drain; the intended path. unsupported — the Querier exposed no raw connection, so nothing could be closed and the DSN's ReadTimeout is the only bound left on the drain. close_error — the raw-connection callback or the Close itself failed, so the drain very likely still happened. Anything other than discarded is worth alerting on: the byte budget stops bounding what crosses the wire, and the symptom is pool exhaustion rather than an error anyone would connect back to sampling.

panels.title: Content Bugs (count, 5m)
panels.description: producer panics — a streaming producer panicked and was recovered; the requester is told INTERNAL/retryable and the message is redelivered, so nothing in the request's own outcome says this connector crashed. byte mismatch — the stored size disagreed with what was sampled and streamed; the handler NAKs without replying, so one count is a transient a redelivery repaired, while a repeating one means the same URN fails verification every attempt and once MaxDeliver is spent the object proven wrong stays under that URN with no reply ever sent.

panels.title: Content Connections (Open) by Pod
