panels.description: Per-pod so one replica leaking connections stands out from the aggregate.

options.content:
### MySQL Connector — Runtime
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/mysql/mysql-runtime.json` · per-cluster board: [MySQL Connector — Runtime](/d/apps-v2-mysql-runtime)

panels.title: Container CPU Usage
panels.description: cAdvisor series, so it is selected by pod name rather than by job — the Component variable does not filter this panel.

panels.title: Container Memory (working set)
panels.description: cAdvisor series, so it is selected by pod name rather than by job — the Component variable does not filter this panel. This is the number the OOM killer watches, not process RSS.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: A count that climbs and never comes back down across scans is the leak signature — the leaf worker pool and the content streaming producers are the two places goroutines are spawned per unit of work.

panels.title: GC Pause (max / p75)
panels.description: go_gc_duration_seconds is a SUMMARY, not a histogram — there is no _bucket series, so histogram_quantile against it returns nothing. These are the pre-computed quantiles the Go collector exports; the available ones are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, so there is no p99 to plot. The label is matched with =~ because client_golang formats these values as "0.0"/"1.0" here while older versions emit "0"/"1" — an exact quantile="1" silently returns nothing.

panels.title: GC Cycles (rate)
panels.description: Completed GC cycles per second, from the summary's observation count. A rate that climbs alongside flat heap in-use means allocation churn rather than growth.

panels.title: Open vs Max FDs
panels.description: Every pooled MySQL connection is a socket, so an open count converging on max is how connection-pool exhaustion presents at the process level.

options.content:
### PostgreSQL Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/postgresql/postgresql-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [PostgreSQL Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-postgresql-overview)

**Totals add up every scan in the time range.** Two scans of a 139-table server read 278 tables. To count what the server holds, narrow the range to one scan.

**Bars and stats say _how many_. The line charts beside them say _when_.** A scan shorter than ~30 seconds can be invisible on a line chart and still be fully counted in the bars.

**One item = one column.** PostgreSQL sends no table documents, so Items Sent should equal Columns Found exactly.

**What this board cannot tell you:** anything per datasource, per database or per schema (the metrics carry none of those labels — the dead-letter messages and the logs do name them); how many connections PostgreSQL is holding (nothing measures it); and how long a scan took end to end (nothing times it: 'Scan Duration' is read off the first and last activity, ±15 s).

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Duration ±15s
panels.description:
**How long the scan took, end to end**: from the moment its databases were listed to the last table read. With several scans in the range it spans all of them, idle gaps included.

**Normal:** seconds to minutes, precise to about ±15 s: it is read from samples taken every 10–30 s, not timed. **0 s means the whole scan fit between two samples** — it ran and was fast (a 144-table server scans in about a second); the counts beside it show what it did.

**Next:** 'Fan-out over time' in the Scanner row shows the same span as a shape.

targets.expr: max_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s]) - min_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s])

panels.title: Databases
panels.description:
**Databases the scan found on the server** and handed out to be scanned, after the configured exclusions.

**Normal:** the number of databases the scan account can see, once per scan in the range.

**Next:** 'Database Failures' in Scan Health for the ones that could not be opened.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Schemas
panels.description:
**Schemas found across those databases**, system schemas excluded.

**Normal:** the user schemas of every scanned database.

**Next:** 'Schemas by Scan Mode' in the funnel for how each one was read.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_schemas_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_schemas_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_schemas_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Tables
panels.description:
**Tables, views, materialized views and foreign tables whose columns were read.**

**Normal:** every relation of every scanned schema. A relation with no columns is skipped in bulk mode and counted in table mode.

**Next:** 'Tables by Outcome' in the funnel.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Columns
panels.description:
**Columns read across all scanned tables.** Each one becomes one item.

**Normal:** roughly tables × average width ('Columns per Table' on the Pipeline board).

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Items Sent
panels.description:
**Items handed to the sender for indexing**, one per column. Counted when queued: a batch that then fails to reach the message queue is not subtracted.

**Normal:** exactly Columns Found.

**Next:** 'Items Lost' beside it.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Items Lost
panels.description:
**Columns found but never handed on for indexing**: Columns Found minus Items Sent.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0 means those columns are missing from the index while the scan still finishes green.

**Next:** 'Columns Lost' in Scan Health, and the scanner logs ('buildDocuments', 'Failed to upsert item').

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)) - ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Fetches
panels.description:
**Column samples requested from the content side**, any outcome. Content runs on its own pods, triggered separately from scans.

**Normal:** whatever the downstream classifier asked for; 0 when nothing requested samples.

**Next:** the Content row.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Funnel — Database → Schema → Table → Column → Item
Schema Attempts
panels.description:
**Times a schema was read — attempts, not schemas.** A schema that fails temporarily is retried, up to 5 times, and every try counts here.

**Normal:** equal to Schemas Discovered. Above it means schemas are failing and being retried.

**Next:** 'NATS Redelivered' in the Scanner row and 'Work Lost (DLQ)' beside it.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type=~"bulk_tables|tables_in_schema"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type=~"bulk_tables|tables_in_schema"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type=~"bulk_tables|tables_in_schema"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Items per Column
panels.description:
**Does every column found become an item?**

**Normal:** 100%. Lower means items failed to be built or queued — the scan still looks green.

**Next:** 'Items Lost' for how many.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Batches Published (window)
panels.description:
**Batches of items that actually reached the message queue.** Items are sent 100 at a time, plus one partial batch per schema, so this is roughly Items Sent ÷ 100 + Schemas Discovered.

**Normal:** steady relative to Items Sent. The only trace of a final batch that failed to publish: Items Sent still counts those items, this does not.

**Next:** the scanner logs for 'Failed to flush remaining items'.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(connector_batches_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(connector_batches_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(connector_batches_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Work Lost (DLQ)
panels.description:
**Scan work that failed all 5 attempts and was given up on** in the selected range: a scan request, a whole database or a whole schema — not indexed while the scan reports success.

**Normal:** 0. The board cannot name it; each message in the dead-letter queue does: `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_POSTGRESQL <seq>`.

**Next:** the Dead Letter Queue row at the bottom.

panels.title: Schemas by Scan Mode (window)
panels.description:
**How each schema was read** (scan mode auto). Bulk = two queries for the whole schema, used below 10,000 columns (POSTGRESQL_BULK_THRESHOLD). Table mode = one query per table, run in parallel, for bigger schemas — or when counting the schema's columns failed. Counts attempts: a retried schema counts again.

**Normal:** mostly bulk. Neither is a problem; table mode is just slower per column. A sudden jump in table mode on the same server means counting columns is failing and schemas are falling back — most often because the server ran out of connections (see Scan Health).

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type="bulk_tables"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type="bulk_tables"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type="bulk_tables"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type="tables_in_schema"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type="tables_in_schema"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", query_type="tables_in_schema"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Schemas by Scan Mode (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When schemas were read, by mode**, same colours as the bars beside it.

**Normal:** a bump per scan. A scan shorter than ~30 seconds may not show here at all — the bars still count it.

panels.title: Tables by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every table.** Scanned = its columns were read. Lost = its column query failed (table mode only; in bulk a failure loses the whole schema, see Scan Health). Permissions missing = scanned, but its column permissions could not be read, so its items went out with empty permissions — a subset of scanned.

**Normal:** only green. Orange needs a grant for the scan account; red needs a look at the scanner logs.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_permissions_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_permissions_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_permissions_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Tables by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When tables were scanned or lost**, same colours as the bars beside it.

**Normal:** a green bump per scan.

**Next:** the bars beside it for how many.

panels.title: NATS Backlog
panels.description:
**Work waiting in the queue** (stream JE_POSTGRESQL): scan requests, databases and schemas not picked up yet. This is 'how far behind is it?', and it is readable even while the connector is asleep.

**Normal:** 0 between scans. Growing with no pods running means the connector is not waking up.

panels.title: NATS In Flight
panels.description:
**Work handed to a pod and not finished yet.** Each message is a whole database or schema.

**Normal:** a few while a scan runs, 0 otherwise. Stuck above 0 while nothing is being scanned means a pod is hung.

panels.title: NATS Redelivered
panels.description:
**Work being retried after a failure.** A database or schema is retried up to 5 times before going to the dead-letter queue.

**Normal:** 0. A connector failing and retrying in a loop shows up here and nowhere else.

**Next:** Scan Health for what is failing.

panels.title: Replicas
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running now**, as the autoscaler reports them.

**Normal:** 0 between scans, a few during one.

panels.title: Max Replicas
panels.description:
**The most scanner pods the autoscaler may start** (chart setting autoscaling.maxReplicas, 10 by default).

**Normal:** read it against Replicas: at the ceiling with a growing backlog means the scanner cannot go faster.

panels.title: Backlog Slope (2m)
panels.description:
**How fast the backlog is growing**, in messages per second. This is exactly what one of the autoscaler's rules looks at.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0.5 the autoscaler adds pods.

panels.title: NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**The queue over time.** Pending = waiting, ack pending = being worked on, redelivered = being retried. Each message is a scan request, a database or a schema, so 3 pending can be three entire schemas.

**Normal:** spikes at the start of a scan that drain to 0.

panels.title: KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Pods running, pods wanted, and the ceiling.**

**Normal:** pods stay up ~5–10 minutes after the work ends (cooldown 300 s, scale-down window 300 s, at most half the pods removed per minute). 'It scaled minutes ago and is still the same' is configuration, not a bug.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Scanner pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — the scanner scales to zero between scans. That is not an outage.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Scanner container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. Usually the pod ran out of memory (limit 1 GiB) or failed its health check; the work it held is retried.

**Next:** the Runtime board.

panels.title: Fan-out Mean
panels.description:
**Only the first step of a scan: connecting, listing the databases and queuing them.** It is NOT how long the whole scan took — databases and schemas are scanned afterwards, possibly on other pods.

**Normal:** well under a second.

**Next:** 'Duration ±15s' in Totals for the whole scan.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_scan_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_scan_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_scan_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_scan_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_scan_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_scan_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Peak In Flight /20
panels.description:
**Most tables this pod was reading at the same time.** Up to 10 schemas at once (POSTGRESQL_NATS_WORKERS), and in table mode up to 10 more tables on the worker pool (POSTGRESQL_POOL_WORKERS) — 20 in all.

**Normal:** below 20. Sampled every 10–30 s, so a small scan can read 0 here and still have run.

**Next:** 'Tables In Flight by pod' in the Queries row.

panels.title: Query p95 (window)
panels.description:
**How slow the slowest 5% of the scanner's SQL queries were**, all kinds together.

**Normal:** under a second on a healthy database.

**Next:** 'Query Time by Type' below, and the Pipeline board for each kind.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) >= 0

panels.title: Queries Run (window)
panels.description:
**SQL queries the scanner sent to PostgreSQL**, all kinds.

**Normal:** about 2 per table plus a few per schema: every table gets a permissions query, and in table mode a column query too.

**Next:** 'Query Count by Type' on the Pipeline board.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Scanner Throughput (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**How fast the scanner is working**, while it works.

**Normal:** only meaningful during a long scan; a short one may read 0 here and still be fully counted in the stats above.

panels.title: Fan-out over time (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When the scan ran.** Databases are discovered first, then schemas, then tables; the span from the first to the last movement of 'tables scanned' is the closest thing to how long the whole scan took.

**Normal:** three bumps in that order, close together.

panels.title: KEDA — Scanner Trigger Signals
panels.description:
**What the scanner's autoscaler looks at.** ack-capacity = work in progress; trend-based = is the queue growing; pending-wakeup = wakes the scanner from zero on the first queued message.

**Normal:** far below the thresholds in the legend. Note the scale: the trend signal is a rate and is tiny next to the others.

panels.title: Query Time by Type (window)
panels.description:
**Where the scanner spent its database time**: total seconds per kind of query. table_permissions runs once per table in both modes; list_columns once per table in table mode; bulk_tables + bulk_columns once per schema in bulk mode; the rest once per database or schema.

**Normal:** table_permissions or list_columns on top — they run per table. A per-schema query on top means one schema is very large.

**Next:** the Pipeline board has each kind's percentiles and counts.

targets.expr: sum by (query_type) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Tables In Flight by pod
panels.description:
**Tables each pod was reading at once**, highest value in each minute. The red line is the per-pod ceiling (20).

The board cannot show connections to PostgreSQL: nothing measures them. For sizing, each scan opens a pool of up to 20 connections per database it reads, per pod, and closes idle ones after ~2.5 minutes — so many databases or many pods can reach the server's max_connections (100 by default) long before this line reaches 20. Measured locally: 15 concurrent scans of a 7-database server filled 100 connections in 2 seconds — all of them idle, held by the scans' pools — and kept the server full for ~3 minutes; 2 scans and 42 databases ended in the dead-letter queue.

**Normal:** below the line. At the line with a growing backlog means the pod is the bottleneck.

**Next:** pg_stat_activity on the server for the real connection count.

panels.title: Start Failures
panels.description:
**Attempts at starting a scan that failed**: could not connect to the server, verify the connection, or list its databases. Each try counts: the scan request is retried up to 5 times, so one scan that never starts reads 5, and then the whole scan is lost.

**Normal:** 0. Usually wrong host, password or network policy — the scan shows as failed in the UI.

**Next:** the scanner logs ('postgresql.connection.*', 'postgresql.database.list_failed').

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="server"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="server"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="server"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Database Failures
panels.description:
**Attempts at reading a database that failed**: its schemas could not be listed. The most common cause is a database the scan account has no CONNECT privilege on — the failure only shows when the first query runs. Each database is retried up to 5 times, so one lost database reads 5 here and 1 in 'Work Lost (DLQ)'.

**Normal:** 0. Any value is an entire database missing from a scan that otherwise finishes.

**Next:** the scan's error list in the UI names the database ('postgresql.schema.list_failed'). Many at once, across several scans, together with Scan Start Failures and a jump in table-mode schemas, is the server refusing connections ('too many clients'): see 'Tables In Flight by pod'.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="database"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="database"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="database"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Schema Failures
panels.description:
**Attempts at reading a schema that failed**: listing its tables failed, or (bulk mode) reading all its columns at once failed. Retried up to 5 times, so one lost schema reads 5.

**Normal:** 0. In bulk mode one lost schema is every one of its tables.

**Next:** 'Errors by What Was Lost' below; the DLQ row if they were retried 5 times.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)) + ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Tables Lost
panels.description:
**Tables whose column query failed** (table mode only). Not retried: the rest of the schema continues, so each one is a distinct table.

**Normal:** 0.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Columns Lost
panels.description:
**Columns that could not be turned into an item or queued.** The table is still counted as scanned.

**Normal:** 0. Anything else means columns missing from the index on a green scan.

**Next:** 'Items Lost' covers these and any other gap between Columns Found and Items Sent.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Permissions Missing
panels.description:
**Tables whose column permissions could not be read.** Their items were still sent, with empty permissions — nothing errors, and access-based classification sees nobody with access.

**Normal:** 0. Usually the scan account cannot read the grant catalog for that schema: grant it, or scan with an owner role.

**Next:** the scanner logs ('Failed to extract permissions').

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_permissions_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_permissions_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_permissions_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Errors by What Was Lost (window)
panels.description:
**Every error, by what it cost the scan.** server = the whole scan. database = one database. schema = one schema. table = one table. One error can be a whole database, so read the label before the length of the bar.

**Normal:** empty. Retries count again: a schema retried 5 times reads 5.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="server"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="server"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="server"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="database"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="database"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="database"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)) + ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="table"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Errors by What Was Lost (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When errors happened**, same colours as the bars beside it.

**Normal:** flat at 0.

targets.expr: ((sum(rate(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[5m]))) or vector(0)) + ((sum(rate(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go", scope="schema"}[5m]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Content pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — content also scales to zero.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Content container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. The memory limit is 512 MiB.

**Next:** the Runtime board.

panels.title: Fetches
panels.description:
**Column samples requested**, any outcome.

**Normal:** whatever was asked for.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome' below.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Content Fetch — mean / p95
panels.description:
**How long one sample takes**, end to end, failures included. Mean = the typical one; multiply by the number of columns to estimate a bigger job. p95 = the slowest 5%.

**Normal:** well under a second. Sampling reads a share of the whole TABLE (10%, at least 100 and at most 10,000 rows), so every column of a big table is slower.

**Next:** the Pipeline board for the distribution.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) >= 0

panels.title: Errors
panels.description:
**Samples that did not succeed**, for any reason.

**Normal:** 0, but not every error is a problem — see the colours in the breakdown.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content", success="false"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content", success="false"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content", success="false"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Fetch Backlog
panels.description:
**Bulk sample requests waiting** (the classifier's queue).

**Normal:** 0 between jobs.

panels.title: Interactive Backlog
panels.description:
**'See content' requests waiting** — a person in the UI is waiting on each of these.

**Normal:** 0 almost always. Anything else means someone is staring at a spinner.

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every sample request.** Green = fine. Yellow = expected (the column or table no longer exists, or the sample is over 100 MB). Orange = configuration (bad request, credential, permission). Red = needs a look. 'reply not sent (retried)' = the sample was uploaded but the answer could not be sent, so the request goes back to the queue and runs again.

**Normal:** mostly green. **'internal' includes a known connector bug:** sampling a column of a VIEW fails (PostgreSQL cannot sample views), so every view column reads red here while the scan is fine. Materialized views work.

**Next:** the line chart beside it shows when; the content logs name the column.

targets.expr: sum by (error_code) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When samples happened and how they ended**, same colours as the bars beside it.

**Normal:** bursts when a classification job runs.

panels.title: Error Replies Not Sent (window)
panels.description:
**Failed samples whose failure could not be reported back.** The request is dropped anyway (retrying would fail the same way), so whoever asked waits until their own timeout instead of hearing the error.

**Normal:** 0. Anything else points at the message queue, not the database.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_error_reply_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_error_reply_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_error_reply_failed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: NATS — Fetch Redelivered
panels.description:
**Sample requests being retried.** Timeouts, lost connections, failed uploads and replies that could not be sent go back to the queue, up to 3 times in all.

**Normal:** 0.

panels.title: NATS — Content Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**Both content queues over time**: bulk (classifier) and interactive (a person waiting in the UI).

**Normal:** spikes that drain to 0. Each request is tried at most 3 times.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Content pods running, wanted, and the ceiling** (10 by default).

**Normal:** 0 when idle; pods stay ~5–10 minutes after the last request (cooldown 300 s).

panels.title: KEDA — Content Trigger Signals
panels.description:
**What the content autoscaler looks at.** The interactive rule exists so a single 'See content' request wakes the pods even when nothing else is queued.

**Normal:** far below the thresholds in the legend.

panels.title: Rows per Sample — mean
panels.description:
**How many rows went into a successful sample**, on average.

**Normal:** between 100 and 10,000 (POSTGRESQL_CONTENT_MIN_ROWS / MAX_ROWS); fewer only for tables with fewer rows. Far below 100 on big tables means samples are coming back thin.

**Next:** 'Samples by Rows' on the Pipeline board.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_sample_rows_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_sample_rows_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_sample_rows_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_sample_rows_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_sample_rows_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_sample_rows_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Sample Size — mean / p95
panels.description:
**How big the uploaded samples were.**

**Normal:** kilobytes to a few megabytes. Samples over 100 MB are refused (too large).

**Next:** 'Samples by Size' on the Pipeline board.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_bytes_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) >= 0

panels.title: Bytes Uploaded (window)
panels.description:
**Total sample bytes uploaded to the content service.**

**Normal:** Fetches × mean sample size.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_cache_write_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_cache_write_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_cache_write_bytes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Samples Too Large (window)
panels.description:
**Samples refused for being over 100 MB** (content.maxSizeBytes). The column is not classified.

**Normal:** 0. Only very wide values (large text, bytea, json) times many rows get there.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_TOO_LARGE"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_TOO_LARGE"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content", error_code="FETCH_ERROR_TOO_LARGE"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Sample Size — rows and KiB per sample (mean, 5m)
panels.description:
**How big the successful samples were over time**, on average.

**Normal:** steady for the same tables. A drop in rows with the same tables means the sampler is getting fewer rows back.

panels.title: DLQ Depth
panels.description:
**Scan work that was given up on and is sitting in the dead-letter queue now.** Each message is a scan request, a database or a schema that failed 5 times — not indexed while the scan reported success.

**Normal:** 0. To see which: each message names the database / schema and the last error — `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_POSTGRESQL <seq>`.

**Next:** 'Work Lost (DLQ)' in the funnel counts the ones added in the selected range.

panels.title: DLQ Depth over time
panels.description:
**When work started landing in the dead-letter queue.**

**Normal:** flat at 0. A step up marks the moment a scan started losing work.

options.content:
### PostgreSQL Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/postgresql/postgresql-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [PostgreSQL Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-postgresql-pipeline)

**This is the drill-down.** The Overview says *what happened*; this board says *how much it cost* and *how it was distributed*. Nothing here is repeated from the Overview.

**Totals add up every scan in the time range** — narrow the range to one scan to describe one server.

**Time here is database time** — how long the scanner waited on PostgreSQL. Nothing times the connector's own work per table, and queries run in parallel, so a scan takes less wall-clock time than the sum shown here.

**The query type selector** at the top narrows the query panels to one kind of query.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Database Time per Table
panels.description:
**Average time PostgreSQL spent answering the scanner, per table**, in milliseconds: every query of the scan (listings, columns, permissions) divided by tables scanned.

**Normal:** a few to tens of ms. Multiply by the number of tables for the database time of a bigger server; the wall-clock scan is shorter because up to 20 tables per pod run in parallel.

**Next:** 'Query Time by Type' on the Overview for which query dominates.

panels.title: Query p95 by query_type
panels.description:
**How slow the slowest 5% of each kind of query was**, over time.

**Normal:** only readable under sustained load. For a single scan use 'Query Mean by query_type' beside it.

**Next:** the Overview's 'Query Time by Type' for where the time went in total.

panels.title: Query Mean by query_type (5m)
panels.description:
**Average time per query of each kind.** The average is the one that multiplies: average × number of calls = total time.

**Normal:** tens of milliseconds at most; bulk_columns grows with the size of the schema.

panels.title: Query Count by Type (window)
panels.description:
**How many queries of each kind ran** — a count, not time.

**Normal:** list_databases = scans; list_schemas = databases; count_schema_columns = schemas; bulk_tables = bulk schemas; bulk_columns = bulk schemas that have tables; tables_in_schema = table-mode schemas; list_columns = tables read in table mode; table_permissions = every table.

panels.title: Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 by success
panels.description:
**How long samples took, successes and failures apart**, so fast failures do not make successes look quicker than they are.

**Normal:** only readable under sustained load.

**Next:** the heatmap beside it for single requests.

panels.title: Fetch Duration — distribution
panels.description:
**How long each sample took, over time**, any outcome. **How to read it:** time runs left to right, the measured value bottom to top. Each box is 'this many fell in this range, at this moment' — brighter = more; hover a box for the exact count (Value). Colours do not identify individual items.

**Normal:** under a second. Sampling reads a share of the whole table, so the big tables are the high boxes.

**Next:** 'Fetches by Duration' beside it.

### PostgreSQL Connector — Runtime
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/postgresql/postgresql-runtime.json` · per-cluster board: [PostgreSQL Connector — Runtime](/d/apps-v2-postgresql-runtime)

**Is the connector itself healthy?** CPU, memory, Go runtime and file handles for the scanner and content pods. Use the *component* selector at the top to look at one of them.

**Empty is normal:** both deployments scale to zero between jobs, so this board only has data while something runs.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it shows, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Process CPU (rate)
panels.description:
**CPU the connector process uses**, in cores.

**Normal:** near 0 when idle, up to the limit during work (0.5 core for the scanner, 0.25 for content). Pinned at the limit means the pod is being throttled and everything slows down.

**Next:** 'Container CPU Usage' for what Kubernetes sees.

panels.title: Process Resident Memory
panels.description:
**Memory the process is really using** (what is in RAM).

**Normal:** well below the limit (1 GiB scanner, 512 MiB content). A line that only goes up across several scans points at memory that is never released — e.g. the scans a scanner pod keeps cached, with their connection pools, for 30 minutes after their last message (jobContextIdleTTL).

**Next:** 'Container Memory (working set)' for the number Kubernetes compares with the limit.

panels.title: Process Virtual Memory
panels.description:
**Memory the process has reserved**, used or not. Go reserves far more than it uses.

**Normal:** large and flat. Not a useful alarm on its own — use resident memory.

panels.title: Container CPU Usage
panels.description:
**CPU per pod as Kubernetes measures it.** These container panels select pods by name, because Kubernetes' own metrics do not carry the connector's labels.

**Normal:** same shape as Process CPU. At the limit (0.5 core scanner, 0.25 content) the pod is throttled.

panels.title: Container Memory (working set)
panels.description:
**Memory per pod as Kubernetes measures it** — the number it compares with the limit (1 GiB scanner, 512 MiB content).

**Normal:** well below the limit. Reaching it gets the pod killed (OOMKilled) and the work it held is retried.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description:
**How many concurrent tasks the program is running.**

**Normal:** grows during a scan and returns to a low, steady number after. A count that keeps growing between scans is a leak.

panels.title: Heap In-Use
panels.description:
**Memory used by the program's own data.**

**Normal:** rises during work and drops after garbage collection. Steadily rising floors across scans mean something is being kept.

panels.title: GC Pause — max & median
panels.description:
**How long the program stops to clean up memory.** Max = the worst pause, median = a typical one.

**Normal:** milliseconds. Pauses of hundreds of milliseconds mean memory pressure.

panels.title: Open vs Max FDs
panels.description:
**Open files and network connections against the process limit.**

**Normal:** far below the limit. Each PostgreSQL connection is one of these — and it is the closest thing to a connection count this connector has: a scan keeps up to 20 connections per database it reads, per pod, closing idle ones after ~2.5 minutes.

panels.title: OS Threads
panels.description:
**Operating-system threads the program uses.**

**Normal:** a small, steady number. Growing steadily means calls are blocking.

The two legs run concurrently through an io.Pipe, so this reflects the slower of the two at any moment. Replaces the old separate Query Duration and Upload Duration metrics, which can't be measured independently in the streaming architecture.

panels.title: Sample Verify-Empty by Outcome (count, 5m)
panels.description: Count of times the verify-at-100% branch fired during content sampling. outcome="recovered" means phase-1 SAMPLE SYSTEM returned zero rows on a non-empty table and the re-run rescued data — sustained > 0 means SamplePercent is too low for the row distribution. outcome="empty" means the re-run also returned nothing — table is genuinely empty, no action needed. Replaces the old sample_fallback_total metric.

### Oracle Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/oracle/oracle-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [Oracle Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-oracle-overview)

**Totals add up every scan in the time range.** Two scans of a 13-owner database read 26 owners. To count what the database holds, narrow the range to one scan.

**Bars and stats say _how many_. The line charts beside them say _when_.** A scan shorter than ~30 seconds can be invisible on a line chart and still be fully counted in the bars.

**What this board cannot tell you:** anything per datasource or per owner (Oracle's metrics carry neither label — the DLQ messages do name the owner), and how many PDBs were scanned (with a credential to a single PDB, everything here is inside that one PDB).

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Scan Duration ±15 s
panels.description:
**How long the scan took, end to end**: from the moment its owners were queued to the last table read. With several scans in the range it spans all of them, idle gaps included.

**Normal:** seconds to minutes. Precise to about ±15 s, because it is measured from samples taken every 10–30 s — a scan of a few seconds can read 0 s or 15 s. Owners run in parallel, so a small database really does finish in seconds (the local test database: about 5 s).

**Next:** 'Fan-out over time' in the Scanner row shows the same span as a shape.

targets.expr: max_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s]) - min_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s])

panels.title: Objects Scanned
panels.description:
**Tables and views whose columns were read successfully.**

**Normal:** the tables + views of every scanned owner, once per scan in the range.

**Next:** 'Objects Failed' beside it; the funnel splits them by outcome.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Columns Found
panels.description:
**Columns read across all scanned tables and views.** Each one becomes a document.

**Normal:** roughly objects × average width (see 'Columns per Object' on the Pipeline board).

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Documents Sent
panels.description:
**Documents handed on for indexing: one per column, plus one per table or view.** It counts documents sent, not distinct tables — the same table scanned twice is sent twice.

**Normal:** exactly Columns Found + Objects Scanned.

**Next:** 'Documents (window)' in the funnel, to see the two kinds apart.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Documents by kind (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When documents went out**, by kind.

**Normal:** both kinds rise and fall together. One flat while the other moves means a whole index stopped receiving.

panels.title: NATS Backlog
panels.description:
**Work waiting in the queue** (stream JE_ORACLE): scan requests and owners not picked up yet. This is 'how far behind is it?', and it is readable even while the connector is asleep.

**Normal:** 0 between scans. Growing with no pods running means the connector is not waking up.

panels.title: NATS In Flight
panels.description:
**Work handed to a pod and not finished yet.**

**Normal:** a few while a scan runs, 0 otherwise. Stuck high while nothing is being scanned means a pod is hung.

panels.title: NATS Redelivered
panels.description:
**Work being retried after a failure.** An owner is retried up to 5 times before going to the dead-letter queue.

**Normal:** 0. A connector failing and retrying in a loop shows up here and nowhere else.

**Next:** 'Objects by Outcome' for what is failing.

panels.title: Replicas
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running now**, as the autoscaler reports them.

**Normal:** 0 between scans, 1–3 during one.

panels.title: Max Replicas
panels.description:
**The most scanner pods the autoscaler may start** (chart setting autoscaling.maxReplicas, 3 by default).

**Normal:** read it against Replicas: at the ceiling with a growing backlog means the scanner cannot go faster.

panels.title: Backlog Slope (2m)
panels.description:
**How fast the backlog is growing**, in messages per second. This is exactly what one of the autoscaler's rules looks at.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0.5 the autoscaler adds pods.

panels.title: NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**The queue over time.** Pending = waiting, ack pending = being worked on, redelivered = being retried. Each message is a scan request or a whole owner, so 3 pending can be three entire schemas.

**Normal:** spikes at the start of a scan that drain to 0.

panels.title: KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Pods running, pods wanted, and the ceiling.**

**Normal:** pods stay up ~15 minutes after the work ends (cooldown 900s, scale-down window 600s). 'It scaled ten minutes ago and is still the same' is configuration, not a bug.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Scanner pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — the scanner scales to zero between scans. That is not an outage.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Scanner container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0.

panels.title: Scanned
panels.description:
**Same number as in Totals**, repeated so this row reads on its own.

**Normal:** see Totals.

panels.description:

panels.description:
**How long scanning one owner takes.** The mean is the typical owner — multiply it by the number of owners to estimate a bigger database. The p95 is how long the slowest 5% of owners took.

**Normal:** mean and p95 close together means owners are similar in size. A p95 several times the mean means a few owners are much bigger than the rest.

**Next:** the 'Owner Duration — distribution' heatmap on the Pipeline board shows them individually.

panels.title: Scanner Throughput (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**How fast the scanner is working**, while it works.

**Normal:** only meaningful during a long scan; a short one may read 0 here and still be fully counted in the stats above.

panels.title: Fan-out over time (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When the scan ran.** The span from the first to the last movement of 'objects scanned' is the closest thing to how long the whole scan took — nothing measures it directly.

**Normal:** fork attempts on top of owners published. Fork attempts above it means owners are being retried.

panels.title: Owner Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
**Owner scan time over time**, as percentiles.

**Normal:** only readable under sustained load. For a single scan use the mean / p95 stat above.

panels.title: Work In Flight
panels.description:
**How much the pod is working on at once**: scan requests, owners and tables. Highest value seen in each minute.

**Normal:** owners at most NATS_WORKERS (10) per pod, tables at most ORACLE_POOL_WORKERS (10). Values are sampled every ~10-30s, so very short bursts can be missed.

panels.title: KEDA — ack-capacity signal vs threshold
panels.description:
**One of the autoscaler's rules: work in progress against its threshold** (red line, 1000). Crossing it asks for another pod.

**Normal:** far below the line.

panels.title: KEDA — trend-based signal vs threshold
panels.description:
**Another autoscaler rule: is the queue growing?** Above the red line (0.5 messages/s) it adds pods.

**Normal:** 0. A third rule wakes the scanner from zero on the first queued message — that is the backlog panel above.

panels.title: Peak Connections /20
panels.description:
**Most connections to Oracle this pod held at the same time.** Each scan opens its own set of up to 20 connections (NATS_WORKERS + ORACLE_POOL_WORKERS, 10 + 10), and keeps idle ones for ~2.5 minutes after it ends.

**Normal:** at most 20 × the number of scans running at once. The real limit is the database's own session limit, which we do not control: past it Oracle refuses connections (ORA-12516), tables fail as 'transient' and owners end up in the dead-letter queue. Measured locally: 30 scans at once → 114 connections → 123 owners lost.

**Next:** 'Job Contexts Active' beside it is the multiplier.

panels.title: Job Contexts Active
panels.description:
**Scans this pod is keeping in memory** — not connections. Each one keeps its own connections: one set, or one more per PDB on a multi-PDB database. They are only dropped on errors or when the pod stops, so this grows by one per scan.

**Normal:** the number of scans this pod has run since it started. Connections ≈ this × (1 + PDBs) × up to 20.

**Next:** 'Peak Connections /20' beside it.

panels.title: Peak In Use
panels.description:
**Most connections actually running a query at the same time.**

**Normal:** below 20. Sampled every ~10-30s, so a small scan can read 0 here and still have used connections.

panels.title: Query p95 (window)
panels.description:
**How slow the slowest 5% of the scanner's SQL queries were**, all kinds together.

**Normal:** under a second or two on a healthy database.

**Next:** 'Query Time by Type' below, and the Pipeline board for each kind's percentiles.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.title: Connection Errors
panels.description:
**Failures setting up a scan's connection to Oracle**: fetching the credentials, connecting, or checking permissions.

**Normal:** 0. NOT where an overloaded database shows up: a connection refused in the middle of a scan counts as a temporary table failure instead.

**Next:** 'Objects by Outcome' and 'Peak Connections /20'.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_connection_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_connection_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_connection_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Publish Retries
panels.description:
**Times queuing an owner failed and had to be retried.** Retries stop after 10 minutes (ORACLE_PUBLISH_TIMEOUT) and the whole scan is retried.

**Normal:** 0. This is the early warning before that happens.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_publish_retries_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_publish_retries_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_publish_retries_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Connection Pool — open / in use / idle
panels.description:
**Connections to Oracle over time**, all of this pod's scans together. The red line is one scan's ceiling (20).

**Normal:** 'open' above the line just means several scans are alive — that sum is what the database has to serve. 'in use' pinned at the line while tables are in flight means the connections, not the connector, are the bottleneck.

panels.title: Query Time by Type (window)
panels.description:

panels.description:

panels.description:

**Normal:** 0.

panels.description:

**Normal:** LONG and LONG RAW on old schemas; anything else is worth a look.

panels.title: DLQ Depth
panels.description:
**Scan work that was given up on and is sitting in the dead-letter queue now.** Each message is a scan request or a whole owner that failed 5 times — a whole schema not indexed while the scan reported success.

**Normal:** 0. To see which owners: each message names the owner and the last error — `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_ORACLE <seq>`.

**Next:** 'Owners in DLQ' in the funnel counts the ones added in the selected range.

panels.title: DLQ Depth over time
panels.description:

**Normal:** flat at 0. A step up marks the moment a scan started losing owners.

options.content:
### Oracle Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/oracle/oracle-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [Oracle Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-oracle-pipeline)

**This is the drill-down.** The Overview says *what happened*; this board says *how much it cost* and *how it was distributed*. Nothing here is repeated from the Overview.

**Totals add up every scan in the time range** — narrow the range to one scan to describe one database.

**Heatmaps show one cell per owner or per query**, so a single slow one stands out instead of disappearing into an average.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Time per Object
panels.description:
**Average time to scan one table or view**, in milliseconds, end to end inside its owner: listing, reading its columns, sending its documents, plus its share of the owner's fixed cost.

**Normal:** a few hundred ms. Multiply by the number of tables to estimate a bigger database. It is the same total time as 'Time per Column' beside it, divided by tables instead of columns — so Time per Object ≈ Time per Column × Columns per Object.

**Next:** 'Time per Column' beside it.

targets.expr: 1000 * sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

panels.title: Time per Column
panels.description:
**The same total time divided by columns instead of tables**, in milliseconds. It is not how long one column takes to read — columns are read together, one query per table.

**Normal:** tens of ms. If it stays flat while Time per Object moves, the tables got wider, not slower.

targets.expr: 1000 * sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

panels.title: Objects per Owner
panels.description:
**Average tables and views per owner**, counting only owners that have some.

**Normal:** any number — but databases are rarely uniform. One big owner hides inside an average.

**Next:** the 'Owner Duration — distribution' heatmap below shows each owner as a cell.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) - ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Columns per Object
panels.description:
**Average width of a table**, in columns.

**Normal:** any number. A very wide table (hundreds of columns) moves this and the cost per table together.

panels.title: Owner Duration — distribution
panels.description:
**How long each owner took, over time.** **How to read it:** time runs left to right, duration bottom to top. Each box is 'this many owners took this long, at this moment' — the colour says how many (brighter = more), and hovering a box shows the exact number as Value. Colours do not identify individual owners.

**Normal:** one tight band when owners are similar. Boxes far above the band are the slow owners — the board cannot name them.

**Next:** 'Owners by Duration' beside it gives the same counts for the whole range, easier to read for a single scan.

**Normal:** only readable under sustained load. For a single scan use the mean beside it.

**Next:** the Overview's 'Query Time by Type' for where the time went in total.

**How many queries of each kind ran** — a count, not time. For where the time went, see 'Query Time by Type' on the Overview.
